en: Drifting aimlessly with the colors of autumn
Leaving behind a long scroll of broken cliffs

points.zh: 布萊斯峽谷國家公園 (Bryce Canyon National Park) 位於猶他州的西南部，約六千萬年前布萊斯峽谷一帶是個湖泊，歷經幾百萬年的蒼桑，泥沙和碳酸鈣混成的石灰岩層層累積。l600萬年前的地殼變動，把原始的湖泊抬升到244O公尺以上的高度。不同於大峽谷，布萊斯峽谷并非由中央河流直接切割浸蝕而成。而是科羅拉多河的支流Paria向源侵奪挖掘，斷崖崩潰所致，質地較硬的石灰岩存留聳立，加上經年累月的雨淋風化，以及冰雪寒霜的精雕細琢，形成今日所見色彩繽紛，精巧的岩柱 (Hoodoos) ，岩塔(Pinnacles)，岩洞 (Grottos)和岩壁教堂 (The Cathedral) 等壯麗景觀，以及綿延20多公里氣勢磅礡，盪人胸懷，有如長軸驟然排開的露天大劇場 (The Amphitheater)。布萊斯峽谷有天然石俑殿堂之喻。19世紀摩鬥教徒Ebenezer Bryce在此闢地墾荒，遂稱此地區為布萊斯峽谷。l928年列爲國家公園。
points.en: Bryce Canyon National Park is located in southwestern Utah. About sixty million years ago, the Bryce Canyon area was a lake, and over the following millions of years, layers of limestone formed from mud and calcium carbonate accumulated one upon another. Geological movement 16 million years ago lifted the ancient lakebed to an elevation above 2,440 meters. Unlike the Grand Canyon, Bryce Canyon was not carved and eroded directly by a central river; rather, it was shaped by headward erosion from the Paria River, a tributary of the Colorado River, causing the cliffs to collapse. The harder limestone remained standing, and through centuries of rain, wind erosion, and the fine chiseling of ice, snow, and frost, it formed today's brilliantly colored and delicately carved rock spires (hoodoos), pinnacles, grottoes, and rock-wall "cathedrals," as well as the magnificent open-air amphitheater stretching more than 20 kilometers, unfurling like a long scroll suddenly opened before the viewer. Bryce Canyon has been likened to a natural hall of stone idols. In the 19th century, the Mormon settler Ebenezer Bryce cleared and farmed land here, and the area came to be called Bryce Canyon. It was designated a national park in 1928.

points.zh: 或是穿梭於櫛比鱗次，高可蔽天，氣勢磅礡的岩柱岩林中，或是目眩於紅，白，橙，瑰麗色澤的波動閃爍中，或是仰望雄偉的岩壁大教堂，想像壁龕上精緻的雕刻，聖堂傳出管風琴迴盪的樂曲。當晨曦來臨，峽谷的岩林自薄霧中蘇醒過來，隨旭日漸升，顏色也逐次變化，由灰褐到赫紅，到滿坑滿谷的白玉，珊瑚和瑪瑙，全都閃耀着玉質般溫潤透剔的光芒。至於落日時分的景色，Sunset Point有最佳的視野，一覽色彩和形態的細緻遞變。整片峽谷岩林猶似舞台，上演一齣精彩的戲碼。隨著夕陽的霞光，佈景不斷的更換:城堡聳立了，神殿消隱了，塔樓坍塌了，暮色中，童話的精靈在岩柱石林間飛舞。這樣的劇碼會持續地重演吧 ? 就像過去的千萬年歲月。或許，就在旦夕之間，造物主決定將它收回，拉下了舞台的帷幕。
points.en: Whether weaving among the densely packed, sky-blocking, majestic stone pillars and stone forests, or dazzled by the shimmering, flickering hues of red, white, and orange, or gazing up at the grand rock-wall cathedral, imagining the delicate carvings in its niches and the sound of organ music echoing from the sanctuary — when dawn arrives, the canyon's stone forest awakens from the mist, and as the sun rises the colors change in turn, from ash-brown to blazing red, to a whole valley of white jade, coral, and agate, all glowing with a warm, jade-like translucent light. As for the scene at sunset, Sunset Point offers the best view, taking in the fine gradations of color and form. The whole canyon of stone forest is like a stage on which a splendid drama is performed. As the sunset glow shifts, the scenery keeps changing: castles rise, temples fade away, towers collapse; in the dusk, fairy-tale spirits dance among the stone pillars. Will this drama go on being performed again and again — just as it has for tens of thousands of years past? Or perhaps, in the blink of an eye, the Creator will decide to take it all back and draw down the curtain on this stage.

points.zh: 蘇東坡的《前赤壁賦》如此寫著:「自其變者而觀之，則天地曾不能以一瞬，自其不變者而觀之，則物與我皆無盡。」所以容我們相信，只要科羅拉多高原依然存在，夏季驟雨和冬天冰雪，將持續雕塑多彩多姿的斷崖岩層，石柱深谷,這壯麗的石俑殿堂會一直聳立，風景會愈來愈迷人。
points.en: Su Dongpo wrote in his "Former Ode on the Red Cliff": "Viewed from the perspective of change, heaven and earth cannot remain still even for the blink of an eye; viewed from the perspective of the unchanging, all things and I alike are inexhaustible." So let us believe that as long as the Colorado Plateau endures, summer downpours and winter snow and ice will go on sculpting its brilliantly colored cliff strata, its stone pillars and deep canyons — this magnificent hall of stone monuments will continue to stand, and the scenery will only grow more enchanting.

points.zh:
這首詩是模擬林亨泰的詩「風景No.2」。原詩如下:
防風林   的
外邊   還有
防風林   的
外邊   還有
防風林   的
外邊   還有
然而海   以及波的羅列
然而海   以及波的羅列
「風景No. 2」是林亨泰 (l924 -，彰化北斗人，笠詩刊創始人之一) 最負盛名的代表詩作。這詩在形式上致力於現代主義前衛技巧的實驗，是以文字的圖象排列來表現的「圖象詩」或「符號詩」。此詩是借詩行或意象語句之重複或平行排列，造成無限的空間疊景，意象的綿延不絕。「風景No.2」用字樸實，意象單純，但透過詩人特殊的句型處理，詩行排列後，簡單的兩組意象 : 防風林與海，竟然產生了詩的視覺，音樂，想像和速度的美感，表現了微妙的現代知性的意象美，這也是此詩經久被引述議論的緣由。
points.en:
This poem imitates Lin Heng-tai's poem "Landscape No. 2." The original poem reads as follows:
Windbreak forest / beyond it
there is / more
windbreak forest / beyond it
there is / more
windbreak forest / beyond it
there is / more
And the sea / and the ranks of waves
And the sea / and the ranks of waves
"Landscape No. 2" is the most celebrated representative work of Lin Heng-tai (1924– , born in Beidou, Changhua, one of the founders of the Li Poetry journal). Formally, this poem is dedicated to experimenting with avant-garde modernist techniques, presenting a 'pictorial poem' or 'symbolic poem' arranged through the visual layout of text. The poem uses the repetition or parallel arrangement of lines or imagistic phrases to create an infinite layering of space, an unending extension of imagery. "Landscape No. 2" uses plain language and simple imagery, but through the poet's distinctive syntactic treatment and the arrangement of its lines, the two simple sets of images — windbreak forest and sea — produce a poetic beauty of vision, music, imagination, and speed, expressing a subtle, modern intellectual beauty of imagery. This is why the poem continues to be cited and discussed.
